subject: Order Form: renewal cadence, notice window & Termination for Convenience scope - BlueWave Health
messages:
From: Dana McIntyre <dana@bluewavehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions: auto-renew & termination for convenience

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looks great and the pilot team is excited. Procurement asked me to circle back on a couple of contract items we want clarified before we move the order form to signature: specifically the auto-renew clause and the broad "Termination for Convenience" language in section 9.

Two asks from our side:
- Can the auto-renewal be changed to require 60 days' advance notice rather than 90, or alternatively allow us to opt out for pilots?
- The TFC language as written reads unilateral and open-ended. We need a mutual TFC or, at minimum, a carve-out that preserves prepaid credits and guarantees a minimal wind-down window for in-flight data exports.

I've attached our procurement questionnaire and highlighted the concern (procurement-questionnaire.pdf). CC'ing Elena (legal) who will do the formal review.

Can you share Redwood's typical compromise here? We are hoping to avoid lengthy legal redlines but need to protect the pilot NPI and ongoing integrations.

Thanks,
Dana McIntyre
Senior Procurement Manager
BlueWave Health
[dana@bluewavehealth.com]

---
Attachment: procurement-questionnaire.pdf (pdf)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Dana McIntyre <dana@bluewavehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions: auto-renew & termination for convenience

Hi Dana — really appreciate the clear flag and the questionnaire.

Short answer: we can be flexible and have three pragmatic approaches depending on commercial comfort. My recommendation for pilots is the middle path so the team can move quickly:

1) Self-serve pilots: keep auto-renew but allow a 30-day opt-out window prior to renewal (standard).
2) Paid pilots / commitment: 60-day advance notice for non-renewal (instead of 90).
3) Enterprise commitments: 90-day notice and standard termination economics.

On TFC: Redwood's standard MSA allows either party to terminate for convenience with 60 days' notice; however, for customers with commitments we commonly make TFC mutual and add a wind-down carveout to preserve prepaid credits and provide a 90-day data export period for active integrations.

I've attached a suggested redline to the order form (BF-OF-Redline-v1.docx) that implements the 60-day notice for the scope you're describing and adds the mutual-TFC + wind-down language. Key bullets in the draft:
- Notice window: 60 days for paid pilots or commitments; 30-day opt-out for self-serve pilots.
- Mutual termination for convenience; if either party terminates under TFC while there is a committed spend, Redwood pro-rates refunds for unused months and guarantees a 90-day export period at no additional charge.
- A carve-out that excludes termination from affecting obligations related to data retention, security incident obligations, and regulatory recordkeeping.

Next steps: if that aligns, Karthik from legal can review and Ben can confirm the pricing fallback if we need to add an early-termination fee for reserved capacity. Happy to sync with Elena this week.

Would you be available for a short legal-commercial call Wed 3/3 at 10am PT?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form questions: auto-renew & termination for convenience

Hannah / Ben — quick internal take before we send a formal redline to BlueWave.

Thanks for the proposed compromise; I generally support it but want to tighten the TFC carve to manage our exposure on committed GPU pools and on-prem support obligations. Proposed tweaks:

- Mutual TFC is fine, but add a narrow exception: TFC will not apply to ongoing professional services SOWs tied to migrations or to any reserved-capacity commitments where we already scaled up hardware. For those, termination should trigger a pro-rated early termination fee equal to the remaining committed months at the agreed rate (standard for Dedicated deals).
- Wind-down export window: 90 days is generous — keep it but allow us to charge at cost if usage exceeds a threshold (e.g., sustained ingestion > 2TB/day) during the export period.
- Notice windows: 60 days for paid pilots good. For the 30-day opt-out for self-serve, we need to ensure we have a final invoice cutoff (we typically bill final partial month).

If we're good with that, I'll prepare a short snippet for the MSA and one-paragraph change for the order form. I'll attach the text file with suggested language for legal (tfc-language-suggestion.txt).

On the call Wed 3/3, I can cover the Dedicated exposure and Ben can confirm what early-termination economics look like under the current pricing worksheet.

-Karthik
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Order form questions: auto-renew & termination for convenience

Dana / Elena — thanks for the patience. Quick summary from our side plus proposed contract language to keep things moving.

Summary (commercially aligned):
- For the pilot under deal BW-2027-OF-0091 we propose a 60-day non-renewal notice window for paid pilots; self-serve pilots may opt out with 30 days' notice.
- Termination for Convenience (TFC): mutual TFC with a carveout for reserved capacity and open SOWs. Where reserved capacity has been provisioned, early termination triggers a pro-rated termination fee (remaining committed months * monthly committed rate).
- Redwood commits to a complimentary 90-day data export/wind-down period; if the customer's export consumes infrastructure beyond a reasonable threshold (2TB/day sustained) Redwood reserves the right to recover incremental costs at cost.

Proposed one-paragraph order-form language (for Elena / your counsel):
"Termination for Convenience. Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice; provided, however, that: (a) this section shall not apply to any reserved-capacity commitments or Professional Services Statements of Work, which shall be subject to an early termination fee equal to the unbilled portion of the committed fees; and (b) upon termination, Redwood will provide a complimentary ninety (90)-day export period to enable orderly decommissioning and data retrieval, subject to Redwood's right to recover incremental infrastructure costs where export activity materially exceeds normal usage (e.g., sustained ingestion above 2TB/day)."

Next steps: Elena, if that looks acceptable in principle I suggest redline acceptance and then we issue a DocuSign link with the BF-OF-Redline-v1 attached. If you prefer, Karthik can send a tracked-redline MSA snippet for the legal team.

Proposed meeting: Wed 3/3 10am PT — confirm or suggest an alternate and we'll put calendar invite and dial-in.

Best regards,
